title: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Short title application and commencement

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS)
ORDER, 1977
1. Short title, application and commencement.‑(1) This Order
may be called the Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies (Elections)
Order, 1977.
(2) It shall apply only in
respect of the forthcoming elections to the Houses of Parliament and the
Provincial Assemblies.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Definitions

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS)
ORDER, 1977
2. Definitions.‑In this Order, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context,‑
(al "Commission"
means the Election Commission constituted under the Election Commission Order,
1977;
(b) "Commissioner"
means the Chief Election Commissioner appointed under the Election Commission
Order, 19771
(c) "Constitution"
means the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, which came into
force on the fourteenth day of August, 1973;
(d) "House" means a
House of Parliament; and
(e) all other words and expressions have the same meaning as in the
Sentate (Members from the Federal Capital) Order, 1973 (P. O. No. 12 of 1973),
or. as the case may be, the Senate (Election) Act, 1975 (LI of 1975), or the
Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976), or the Laws
(Continuance in Force) Order, 1977 (C.M.L.A. Order No. 1 of 1977).

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Time of elections

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS)

3. Time of elections.‑‑Elections to the two Houses and
the Provincial Assemblies shall be held in the month of October, 1977, on dates
to be notified by the Commission under the Representation of the People Act,
1976 (LXXXV of 1976), or, as the case may be, under the Senate (Election) Act,
1975, with the prior approval of the President.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
The National Assembly

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS)
ORDER, 1977
4. The National Assembly,‑As provided in Article 5 t of the
Constitu tion‑
(1) the National Assembly shall
consist of two hundred members and the seats therein shall stand allocated to
each Province, the Federally Administered Tribal Areas and the Federal Capital
as provided in section 7 of the Delimitation of Constituencies Act, 1914 (XXXIV
of 1974);
(2) in addition to the number of
seats referred to in paragraph (1)‑
(a) there shall be in the
National Assembly six additional seats reserved for persons belonging, as
referred to in clause (i) of Article 106 of the Constitution, the Christian;
Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist and Parsi communities and persons of the Quadiani group
or Lahori group (who call themselves 'Ahmadis'), and other non‑Muslims
and persons belonging to the scheduled castes; and
(b) in addition to the number
ox seats referred to in paragraph (1), ten seats shall he reserved for women
which shall stand allocated to the Provinces as provided in section 7 of the
Delimitation of Constituencies Act, 1974 (XXXIV of 1974);
(3) for the purpose of election
to the National Assembly, the consti tuencies shall be such as they stood delimited
on the seventh day of March, 1977, and no amendment or modifization shall be
made therein;
(4) as soon as
practicable after the general election to the National Assembly, the members to
&11 seats reserved in that Assembly for the persons referred to in
paragraph (2) shall be elected in accordance with law by the members of the
Assembly referred to In paragraph (1) ;
(5) for the purpose of election to the seats
allocated to a Province under Sub-paragraph (b) of paragraph (2), the members
of the National Assembly from that Province shall constitute the electoral
college; and
(6) notwithstanding anything contained in this
Article, the President may, by Order, make such provision as to the manner of
filling the seats in the National Assembly allocated to the Federally
Administered Tribal Areas as he may think fit.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
The Senate

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS)
ORDER, 1977
5. The Senate.‑(I) As
provided in Article 59 of the Constitution,‑
(a) the Senate shall consist of
sixty‑three members, of whom‑
(i) fourteen shall be elected by the members of each
Provincial Assembly;
(ii) five shall be elected by the members from the
Federally Adminis tered Tribal Areas in the National Assembly; and
(iii) two shall be chosen from the Federal Capital in
such manner a' the President may, by Order, prescribe;
(b) election to fill seats in the Senate allocated to
each Province shall be hold in accordance with the system of proportional
representation by means of the single transferable vote; and
(e) term of office of the members of the Senate shall
be four years, half of them retiring every two years, except in the case of the
members, elected by the members from the Federally Administered Tribal Areas,
of whom three shall retire after the expiration of the first two years and two
shall retire after tire expiration of the next two years;
Provided that the term of office of a person elected
or chosen to fill a casual vacancy shall be the un-expired term of the member
whose vacancy he has filled.
(2) The members elected or chosen as members of the
Senate shall be divided into two groups by drawing lots, the first group
consisting of seven members from each Province, three members from the
Federally Administered ;Tribal Areas and one member from the Federal Capital and
the second group consisting of seven members from each Province, two members
from the said Areas and one member from the Federal Capital.
(3) The term of office of members of the first group
and of the second group shall respectively be two years and four years.
(4) The term of
office of persons elected or chosen to succeed the members of the Senate at
the expiration of Chair respective terms shall be four years.

(2) For the purpose of election to a Provincial

(3) As soon as practicable after the general election
to a Provincial Assembly, the members to fill seats reserved in the Assembly

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Oath of candidates and persons elected

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
7. Oath of candidates and persons elected.‑~I) Every person who is a
candidate for election to a House or a Provincial Assembly, and every person
who is declared to have been elected as a member of a House or a Provincial
Assembly. shall make before such person as may be appointed by the Commission
for the purpose of oath in the form set out in the First Schedule or, as the
case may be, the Second Schedule.
(2) No nomination paper of a
candidate shall be accepted unless it contains the oath referred to in clause
(1) duly made by the candidate as required by that clause.
(3) A person elected to a House or a Provincial
Assembly shall not sit or vote until he has made before the person referred to
in clause (1) oath in the form set out in the Second Schedule.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Duration of an assembly

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
8. Duration of on Assembly.‑As provided respectively in
Articles 52 and 107 of the Constitution, the National Assembly and a Provincial
Assembly shall, unless sooner dissolved, continue for a term of five years from
the day of its first meeting and shall stand dissolved at the expiration of its
term.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Persons qualified to vote

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
9. Persons
qualified to vote.‑(1) At an election to the National Assembly or a
Provincial Assembly, only such persons shall be entitled to vote in a
constituency as stood enrolled on the electoral roll in any electoral area in
that constituency immediately before the commencement of this Order.
(1) Nothing in clause (1) shall be deemed to deprive
an elector of the right to cast his vote because of any defect or error in the
entries in the electoral roll relating to him which is not of a substantial
nature.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Qualifications and disqualifications for membership of Parliament

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
10. Qualifications and disqualifications for membership of Parliament. (1) A person shall
not be qualified to be elected or chosen as member of Parliament unless, as
provided in Article 62 of the Constitution,‑
(e) he is a citizen of Pakistan ;
(b) he is, in the case of the
National Assembly, not less than twenty‑five Years of age and is enrolled
as a voter in any electoral roll for election to that Assembly ; and
(c) he is, in the case of the
Senate, not less than thirty years of age and is enrolled as a voter in any
area in a Province or, as the case may be, the Federal Capital or the Federally
Administered Tribal Areas, from where he seeks membership ;
and has made oath as provided
for fn Article 7.
(2) A person shall be
disqualified from being elected or chosen as, and from being, a member, of
Parliament,‑
(a) if, as provided in Article
63 of the Constitution,‑
(i) he is of unsound mind and
has been so declared by a competent .Court ; or
(2) he is an undischarged
insolvent ; or
(3) he ceases to be a citizen
of Pakistan, or acquires the citizenship of a foreign State ; or
(4) he holds an office of
profit in the service of Pakistan other than an .office declared by law not to
disqualify its holder ; or
(b) if‑
(1) he has been, on conviction
for any offence which in the opinion of ‑the Commissioner involves moral
turpitude, sentenced to imprisonment for a term of rot less than two years,
unless a period of five years has elapsed since his release ; or
(2) he has been dismissed from
the service of Pakistan on the ground of misconduct, unless a period of five
years has elapsed since his dismissal ; on
(3) he has been removed or compulsorily
retired from the service of Pakistan on the ground of misconduct, unless a
period of three years has elapsed since his removal or compulsory retirement ;
or
(4) he has been in the service
of Pakistan or of any statutory body or any body which is owned or controlled
by the Government or in which the Government has a controlling share or
interest, unless a period of two years has elapsed since he ceased to be in such service ; or
(5) he is found guilty of a
corrupt or illegal practice under any other law for the time being in force,
unless a period of five years has elapsed from the date on which that order
takes effect ; or
(6) he has, at any time on or after the twentieth day of December, 1971, been an office‑bearer of a
political party dissolved under subsection (2) of section 6 of the Political Parties Act, 1962
(III of 1962). and has not, before a declaration in respect of such party
is made under subsection (1) of that section, resigned, or publicly announced
his dissociation, from such party, unless a period of five years has elapsed
from the date of such dissolu tion ; or
(7) he has been convicted under
section 7 of the Political Parties Act, 1962 (III of 1962), unless a period of
five years has elapsed from the data of such conviction ; or
(8) if he, whether by himself
or by any person or body of parsons in trust for him or for his benefit or on
his account or as a member of a Hindu undivided family, has any share or
interest in a contract, not being A contract between a cooperative society and
Government, for the supply of goods to, or for the execution of any contract or
the performance of any services undertaken by. Government ;
Provided that the
disqualification under this paragraph shall not apply to a person‑
(i) where the share or interest
in the contract devolves on him by inheritance or succession or as a legatee,
executor or administrator, until the expiration of six months after it has so
devolved on him or such longer period as the President may, in any particular
case, allow ; or
(ii) where the contract has
been entered into by or on behalf o

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Qualifications and disqualifications for membership of Provincial Assembly

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
11. Qualifications and disqualifications for membership of Provincial
Assembly.‑(1) A person shall not be qualified to be elected as member
of a Provincial Assembly unless, as provided in Article 113 of the
Constitution,‑
(a) he is a citizen of Pakistan
;
(b) he is not less than twenty‑five
years of age ;
(c) he is enrolled as a voter
in an electoral roll for election to the Assembly ;
and has made oath as provided
for in Article 7.
(2) A person shall be
disqualified from being elected as, and from being, a member of a Provincial
Assembly if he is subject to any of the disqualifica tions specified in clause
(2) of Article 10.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Bar against double membership

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
12. Bar against double membership.‑(1) As provided in
Article 223 of the Constitution, no person shall at the same time, be a member of‑
(a) both houses ; or
(b) a House and a Provincial
Assembly ; or
(c) the Assemblies of two or
more Provinces ; or
(d) a House or a Provincial
Assembly in respect of more than one seat.
(2) Nothing in clause (1) shall
prevent a person from being a candidate for two or more seats at the same time,
whether in the same body or in different bo‑dies, but if he is elected to
more than one seat he shall, within a period of thirty days after the
declaration of the result for the last such seat, resign all but one of the
seats, and if he does not so resign, all the. seats to which he has been
elected shall become vacant at the expiration of the said period of thirty days
except the seat to which he has been elected last or, if be has been elected to
more than one seat on the same day, the seat his election to which was declared
last.
Explanation.‑In this
clause "body" means either House or a Provincial Assembly.
(3) A person to whom clause (2)
applies shall not take a seat in either House or the Provincial Assembly to
which he has been elected until he has resigned all but one of his seats.
(4) If a member of either House
or of a Provincial Assembly becomes a candidate for a second seat which, in
accordance with clause (1), he may not hold concurrently with his first seat,
then his first seat shall become vacant as soon as he is elected to the second
seat.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Power of commission to declare a poll void

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
13. Power of Commission to declare a poll void.‑(1) If, from
facts apparent on the face of the record or after such summary inquiry as it
deems necessary. the Commission is of the opinion that, by reason of grave
irregularities or violation of the provisions of the Representation of the
People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976), or the rules made thereunder, the poll in any
constituency ought to be declared void, the Commission may make a declaration
accordingly, and, by notification in the official Gazette, call upon that
constituency to elect a member in the manner provided for in section 108 of the
said Act.
(2) The Commission may exercise
the power conferred on it by clause (1) at any time before the name of the
returned candidate has been published under subsection (4) of section 42 of the
Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976), or within one hundred
and twenty days of such publication.
(3) A case taken up by the
Commission and pending before it at the expiration of the period specified in
clause (2) shall not abate and shall be decided by the Commission.
(4) While exercising the powers
conferred on it by clause (i), the Commission shall be deemed to be a tribunal
to which an election petition has been presented and shall, notwithstanding
anything contained in Chapter VII of the Representation of the People Act, 1976
(LXXXV of 1976), regulate Its own procedure.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Election dispute

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
14. Election dispute.‑Save as provided in Article 13, no election
to a House or a Provincial Assembly shall be called in question except by an
election petition presented to such tribunal and in such manner as is provided
for in the Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976).

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Declaration of result

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
15. Declaration of result.‑(I) The Presiding Officer shall,
immediately after the count, declare the provisional result of the count.
(2) The Commission shall,
subject to the provisions of Article 13, publish the name of each returned
candidate in the official Gazette within fifteen days of the polling day.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Election laws applicable

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
16. Election laws applicable.‑The Senate (Members from Federal
Capital) Order, 1973 (P. O. No 12 of 1972), the Senate (Election) Act, 1975 (LT
of 1975), and the Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976), and
any rules made thereunder shall, in so far as they are not inconsistent with
any of the provisions of this Order, apply to the choosing of a member from the
Federal Capital and to the conduct of elections to the two Houses and the
Provincial Assemblies.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Summoning of assemblies

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
17. Summoning of Assemblies.‑(1) Within thirty days of the
polling day, the President shall summon the National Assembly, and the Governor
of a Province shall summon the Assembly for that Province, to meet at such time
and place as he thinks fit.
(2) The Commissioner shall
preside at all meetings of the National Assembly, and a member of the
Commission nominated by the Commissioner shall preside at all meetings of a
Provincial Assembly, convened under this Order.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Elections to reserved seats

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
18. Elections to reserved seats.‑The National Assembly and a
Provincial Assembly shall, at its first meeting and to the exclusion of any
other business, elect the members to fill the seats reserved in that Assembly
for the persons referred to in paragraph (2) of Article 4 or, as the case may
be, paragraph (b) of clause (1) of Article 6, or for woman.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Election of members of senate

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
19. Election of members of Senate.‑(1) As soon
ate may be after the National Assembly has elected members to the reserves
seats referred to in Article 18‑
(a) the member of the National
Assembly from the Federally Adminis tered Tribal Areas shall elect five members
to the Senate ; and
(b) the members of the National Assembly shall choose two members
of the Senate from the Federal Capital.
(2) As soon as may be after a
Provincial Assembly has elected members to the reserved seats referred to in
Article 18, it shall elect fourteen members of the Senate.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Joint sitting of Parliament

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
20. Joint sitting of
Parliament.‑(1) After the elections referred to in Articles 18 and 19
have been held, the President may summon both Houses in joint sitting to meet
at such time and place as he thinks fit and may also prorogue the same.
(2) The President shall preside
at a meeting of the two Houses in joint sitting and, after his Presidential
address, may call upon the Chief Martial Law Administrator to address the joint
sitting.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Election of speaker and deputy speaker

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
21. Election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker.‑(1) After the
joint sitting, if any, is prorogued under Article 20, the President shall
summon the National Assembly and the Governor of a Province shall summon the
Assembly for the province.
(2) At its first meeting after
being summoned under clause (1), the National Assembly and each Provincial
Assembly shall, to the exclusion of any other business, elect from amongst its
members a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Election of prime minister and chief ministers

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
22. Election of Prime
Minister and Chief Ministers.‑(1) As provided in Article 91 of the
Constitution, after the election of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, the
National Assembly shall, to the exclusion of any other business, proceed to
elect without debate one of its Muslim members to be the Prime Minister.
(2) The Prime Minister shall be
elected by the votes of the majority of the total membership of the National
Assembly:
Provided that, if no member,
secure: such majority in the first poll, a second poll shall be held between
the members who secure the two highest numbers of votes in the first poll and
the member who secures a majority of votes of the members present and voting
shall be declared to have been elected as Prime Ministers;
Provided further that, if the
number of votes secured by two or more members securing the highest number of
votes is equal, further poll shall be held between them until one of them
secures a majority of votes of the members present and voting.
(3) The provisions of clauses
(1) and (2) shall apply to the election of a Chief Minister as if reference
therein‑
(a) to "Article 91" were a reference to "Article
131" ;
(h) to the "National
Assembly" were a reference to the "Provincial Assembly" I
(c) to "Muslim
members" were a reference to "members"
(d) to the "Prime
Minister" were a reference to the "Chief Minis ter" ; and
(e) to the
"President" were a reference to the "Governor".

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Revocation of proclamation

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
23. Revocation of Proclamation.‑After the elections referred to
in Articles 21 and 22 have been held, the Chief Martial Law Administrator will
issue a proclamation revoking the proclamation of the fifth day of July, 1977,
for withdrawing Martial Law.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Election to be deemed to be held under constitution

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
24. Election to 6e deemed to be held under Constitution.‑‑‑The elections held
under this Order to the Houses and the Provincial Assemblies and to the offices
of Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Chief Minister shall be deemed
to have been held under the Constitution and shall have effect accordingly.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Power to make rules

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
25. Power to make rules.‑The
President may, by notification in the official Gazette, may make rules for
carrying out the purposes of this Order.

sections.shortTitle: Houses of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Elections Order 1977
sections.description:
Removal of difficulties

PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION) ORDER 5 OF 1977
PRESIDENT'S (POST PROCLAMATION)
ORDER 5 OF 1977
HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1977
26. Removal of difficulties.‑If stay difficulty arises in giving
effect to any of the provisions of this Order, the President may make such
provision for the removal of the difficulty as he may deem fit.
